rationale: 切り詰め量 denotes the amount trimmed away, rather than remaining image size. The argument followed by の makes a grammatical Japanese field label for each specific edge.
Current edge arguments are 左, 上, 右, 下. Expected formatted labels are 左の切り詰め量（%）, 上の切り詰め量（%）, 右の切り詰め量（%）, 下の切り詰め量（%）. These are static predictions, not observed runtime outputs.
The percent sign in full-width parentheses clearly identifies the percentage unit. It is semantically equivalent here to 百分率 and does not imply pixels. The separate pixel label explicitly uses ピクセル.

ImageCropDialog builds four edge fields and switches their contentDescription to this key when percent is true; initial fields use the pixel key. Percentage display arithmetic uses horizontal margins / original width and vertical margins / original height, times 100. This is coherent with a trim-amount percentage label, not a retained-size label.

The indexed string argument %1$s is preserved exactly once. In LocaleText.tokens, %% is a literal token with no argument index. resolve compares argument-bearing contracts only, so the added literal percent does not add an argument or conflict with the source contract. String.format then renders %% as a single percent sign.

This conclusion was reached from the current Japanese phrase, actual consumer, and formatter; the previous acceptance and compatibility review are not used as proof of independent current wording acceptance.
